author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected in place, without booking a second visit and without cancelling the first. A correction is validated exactly as a booking is: description required, date later than today.
acceptance_criteria: GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit renders the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template with the visit model attribute prefilled from the visit's current date and description

POST to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit with a valid description and a date later than today updates the same visit in place, creates no additional visit record, and redirects to the owner detail page
POST with a blank description is refused, names the description field, and redisplays the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template
POST with a date of today or earlier is refused, names the date field, and redisplays the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template
the owner detail page gains no link to the correction; the edit endpoint is reachable by URL only in this slice
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-4, NG-5)
adding a correction link to the owner detail page or any other UI entry point to the edit endpoint
notes: Product decisions are final for this slice. Open question recorded in the PRD: how a reader discovers the correction is deferred; the endpoint is intentionally reachable by URL only. Narrowest reading taken where unspecified: the correction reuses booking's validation and its GET/POST prefill-and-redisplay behavior, and a visit that does not belong to the named owner/pet is refused as booking already is (Visits edge case 1).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the existing edit-in-place-through-the-aggregate-root pattern to visits. Correcting a Visit reuses the exact mechanism owner-edit and pet-edit already use: a non-new entity reached through the eagerly-fetched Owner graph is the form-binding target, and OwnerRepository.save(owner) cascades it as a JPA UPDATE rather than an INSERT (system-design.md #persistence and #state-machine — 'branch on isNew() to choose insert vs update', open-in-view disabled so associations are eager). No VisitRepository, no service layer, no new persistence mechanism, no new dependency. The small adjustments: (1) an aggregate-root read accessor on Owner to resolve a Visit by pet id + visit id, mirroring the existing Owner.getPet(Integer id) and Owner.addVisit(petId, visit) so access stays through the root (DDD aggregate discipline, system-design.md #overview); (2) VisitController's @ModelAttribute('visit') becoming visitId-aware so the edit flow binds onto the EXISTING visit instead of a fresh one. The product decision is already recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md (correction in, cancellation out, updated in place); no architectural ADR is warranted. Basis: read of Owner.java, Pet.java, Visit.java, VisitController.java, and createOrUpdateVisitForm.html directly (IntelliJ oracle not connected on this run — file reads are the basis, stronger than grep).
integration_points: GET+POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit added to VisitController alongside the existing /visits/new routes

VisitController.@ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit must distinguish new-vs-edit: for the edit routes it must return the EXISTING visit resolved by visitId (so binding mutates it in place and the form prefills from its current date/description), and must NOT call pet.addVisit(new Visit()) which would create a second record. Simplest realization: accept @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId; when present, resolve the existing visit; when absent, keep today's new-visit behavior

New accessor on the Owner aggregate root to resolve a visit by (petId, visitId) — e.g. Owner.getVisit(Integer petId, Integer visitId) — iterating pet.getVisits() by BaseEntity id, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id). This is why Owner.java is a file target

POST edit handler reuses processNewVisitForm's validation verbatim: @Valid Visit triggers @NotBlank description; controller adds result.rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate') when date is null-or-not-after-today; on errors return 'pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm'; on success owners.save(owner) then redirect:/owners/{ownerId}

Owner/pet/visit ownership mismatch (Visits edge case 1 per prd-entry notes): the @ModelAttribute loader already throws IllegalArgumentException when the pet is absent for the owner; extend the same refusal when the visit is absent for that pet

patterns.description: processNewVisitForm — the validation block (non-future date rejection + @Valid) and the save+redirect the edit POST mirrors exactly
Owner.getPet(Integer id) — the by-identity aggregate-root accessor the new getVisit accessor mirrors; addVisit(petId, visit) at Owner.java:164 is the sibling write path
existing edit-in-place-via-cascade-save flow (pet correction) — the precedent that a non-new entity saved through OwnerRepository updates rather than inserts

risks.risk: Sharing the @ModelAttribute('visit') method across new and edit routes: if it unconditionally creates a fresh Visit and calls pet.addVisit(...), the edit flow both loses the prefill and inserts a second visit record, failing the in-place AC
risks.mitigation: Make the model-attribute method visitId-aware (required=false path variable). For the edit path return the existing visit from the pet's collection and do not add a new one; assert the in-place behavior with processEditVisitFormUpdatesVisitInPlace (same visit id survives, pet.visits count unchanged)

risks.risk: Template createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is listed as a file target but likely needs no functional change: th:object=${visit} + the inputField fragments already prefill date/description, and the heading/previous-visits already branch on visit['new'] (isNew()), which is false for an existing visit. The form posts to the current URL (no action attribute), so /edit self-posts correctly
risks.mitigation: Verify prefill renders the existing values during the TDD Green step; treat any template edit as cosmetic (e.g. button label) only — do not add a UI entry point, per NG and the URL-only AC. If no functional change is needed, leaving it untouched is correct despite the file-target listing

notes: Not conflicting: docs/adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md is the recorded owner decision that narrows NG-5 and opens REQ-VIS-003, exactly satisfying the 2026-08-08 ADR's requirement that narrowing be a recorded owner decision. Durable-memory writes accompanying this triage: system-design.md Contracts table Implements column extended with REQ-VIS-003 on Owner, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController rows (VisitController purpose now names in-place correction); docs/adr/README.md index gained the missing 2026-08-23 non-goal ADR row. No new ADR authored — the mechanism is the already-sanctioned direct-mapping + cascade-save-through-aggregate pattern with no new trade-off. No design-doc-autofix records present, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Do not add a service layer or a VisitRepository (would breach the recorded feature-package-without-service-layer decision and the aggregate-root write-path invariant).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Object-level authorization enforced through the aggregate root: owner.getVisit(petId, visitId) resolves only visits of a pet owned by the loaded owner, so a visitId from another pet/owner is refused with IllegalArgumentException (no IDOR)
Identity rebinding blocked: @InitBinder setDisallowedFields("id","*.id") prevents a POST parameter from redirecting the update onto a different visit record
In-place update preserved: edit path returns the existing visit and never calls pet.addVisit(...); owners.save(owner) cascades a JPA UPDATE, creating no second record and touching no unrelated data
No injection introduced: persistence via JPA findById only; path variables (int/Integer) interpolate into exception messages, not queries; user text rendered through Thymeleaf auto-escaping

Owner @ModelAttribute binding mirrors the existing processNewVisitForm pattern; the id/*.id disallow-list neutralizes the identity-rebinding vector, and app-wide absence of authentication is the project's pre-existing threat model, not introduced by this slice

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The Javadoc block on loadPetWithVisit was not updated when visitId was introduced. Three concrete errors: (1) @return Pet is factually wrong — the method returns Visit; (2) @param petId carries no description; (3) the new @PathVariable visitId parameter has no @param entry at all. The prose ('make sure that Pet object always has an id') no longer covers the edit-route branch, which now resolves an existing Visit rather than creating one. A future reader encountering this comment will be misled about both the return type and the method's dual-mode behavior.
findings.fix: Replace the stale block with an updated Javadoc that documents all three parameters (ownerId, petId, visitId) with descriptions, states the return type correctly as Visit, and explains the two branches: when visitId is null a fresh Visit is created and added to the pet; when visitId is non-null the existing Visit is resolved through the aggregate root and returned for in-place binding.

approved_aspects: Owner.getVisit(Integer petId, Integer visitId) mirrors getPet(Integer id) exactly — same null-return contract, same isNew() guard, same Objects.equals identity check — consistent with codebase pattern
getVisit Javadoc is accurate: both @param entries and @return are correct, and the link back to getPet(Integer) explains the design intent

@PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) on @ModelAttribute correctly injects null for /visits/new routes, enabling the single loadPetWithVisit method to serve both booking and edit flows without duplication

processEditVisitForm omits owner.addVisit(petId, visit) correctly — the visit is already in the pet collection, so save(owner) cascades the UPDATE; the inline comment makes the in-place contract explicit
Error messages in loadPetWithVisit include owner/pet/visit IDs for operational debuggability
Date validation and @Valid reuse is exact: processEditVisitForm mirrors processNewVisitForm validation block with no divergence
Comment pattern above GET/POST handlers (Spring MVC calls method loadPetWithVisit...) is consistent with the pre-existing style on initNewVisitForm and processNewVisitForm

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All five new test methods use implementation-style names (initEditVisitForm, processEditVisitFormSuccess, processEditVisitFormUpdatesVisitInPlace, processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenDescriptionIsBlank, processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture). The testing-principles.md § Test Naming requires BDD school the{Subject}Should{Outcome} for all tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. These names mirror the production method being called, not the behavior that must be true afterward — a name that would survive renaming the production method is a behavior name; these would not.
findings.fix: Rename to BDD school: theEditVisitFormShouldPrefillExistingValues, theEditVisitFormShouldRedirectOnSuccess, theEditVisitFormShouldUpdateVisitInPlace, theEditVisitFormShouldRefuseBlankDescription, theEditVisitFormShouldRefuseNonFutureDate.

findings.description: The @BeforeEach init() method, which was modified in this slice to seed the existing visit, constructs Owner, Pet, and Visit directly via new. testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction requires all objects be wrapped in factory methods for tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward. This is not pre-existing debt the exemption covers — the method was modified in this slice, so it must move its construction behind factories.
findings.fix: Extract createAnOwner(), createAPet(), and createAVisit(date, description) factory helpers within the test class and replace the raw constructors in init().

findings.description: initEditVisitForm asserts only that the visit's description is prefilled (hasProperty description = 'Existing description') but omits the date. AC #1 reads 'prefilled from the visit's current date and description' — both fields are required. The seeded visit has date = LocalDate.now().plusDays(5); that date prefill is unverified.
findings.fix: Add .andExpect(model().attribute("visit", hasProperty("date", is(LocalDate.now().plusDays(5))))) to the test assertion chain.

approved_aspects: processEditVisitFormUpdatesVisitInPlace genuinely guards the load-bearing risk: it verifies pet.getVisits().hasSize(1) (no additional record created), updated.getId() == TEST_VISIT_ID (same visit id survives), description and date mutated in place — all three load-bearing invariants are independently asserted

All five acceptance criteria are covered in structure: GET prefill (initEditVisitForm), POST success redirect (processEditVisitFormSuccess), in-place update (processEditVisitFormUpdatesVisitInPlace), blank-description refusal (processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenDescriptionIsBlank), non-future-date refusal (processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture)

Error code specificity: processEditVisitFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture asserts model().attributeHasFieldErrorCode('visit','date','typeMismatch.visitDate'), pinning the exact error code rather than just the presence of an error

Mocking usage is consistent with the existing suite's sanctioned pattern: OwnerRepository is a system boundary (database), MockitoBean is the framework's in-process test harness, and real domain objects (Owner, Pet, Visit) are used throughout
AssertJ is used for the post-action in-place assertions in processEditVisitFormUpdatesVisitInPlace; Hamcrest use in model().attribute() is a Spring MVC test API constraint, not a policy violation

No additional test coverage of AC #5 (no link on owner detail page) is expected at this layer — that negative constraint is a template/HTML concern outside the web-layer unit test scope and is noted as a known gap, not a defect in these tests
All five tests pass with the current build (./gradlew test UP-TO-DATE, build-pass at line 6 confirmed)
